    30	| Collection | Path | Mask | Purpose |
    31	|---|---|---|---|
    32	| `pi-memory` | `${PI_MEMORY_DIR:-~/.pi/agent/memory}` | `**/*.md` | Primary live Pi memory (`MEMORY.md`, `SCRATCHPAD.md`, `daily/*.md`). |
    33	| `dream-memory` | `~/obsidian/dream-memory/memory` | `**/*.md` | Optional consolidated dream output. |
    34	| `<repo>-code` | repo root | `**/*.{ts,tsx,js,jsx,py,go,rs,md,json,yml,yaml}` | Source, tests, docs, config for one project. |
    35	| `pi-docs` | Pi docs root | `**/*.md` | Pi SDK/docs/reference when developing extensions. |
    36	| `agent-notes` | curated notes dir | `**/*.md` | Human-maintained operational notes, if separate from dream-memory. |
    37	
    38	Example for this repo:
    39	
    40	```sh
    41	qmd collection add ~/Projects/testing/dream-memory-harness \
    42	  --name dream-memory-harness-code \
    43	  --mask "**/*.{ts,tsx,js,jsx,json,md,yml,yaml}"
    44	
    45	qmd context add qmd://dream-memory-harness-code \
    46	  "Source, tests, docs, and CLI code for the dream-memory-harness project. Use for implementation details and test locations, not durable user preferences."
    47	
    48	qmd context add qmd://dream-memory-harness-code/src \
    49	  "Runtime source: Pi extension, hook dispatcher, event store, active recall, dream phase, and CLI."
    50	
    51	qmd context add qmd://dream-memory-harness-code/tests \
    52	  "Vitest regression tests for extension wiring, active recall, QMD health, dream phase, and CLI commands."
    53	
    54	qmd embed --chunk-strategy auto
    55	```
    56	
    57	## Query mode guidance
    58	
    59	`qmd query` is the best quality mode: lexical BM25 + vector search + local LLM query expansion + reranking.
    60	
    61	Use it for manual investigation and high-quality one-off agent searches:
    62	
    63	```sh
    64	qmd query "before_agent_start cache safety" -c pi-memory --json --explain -n 5
    65	qmd query "active recall circuit breaker" -c dream-memory-harness-code --json --explain -n 5
    66	```
    67	
    68	For the hot active-memory path, prefer the HTTP daemon so models and SQLite stay warm:
    69	
    70	```sh
    71	qmd mcp --http --daemon
    72	export DREAM_QMD_HTTP_PORT=8181
    73	```
    74	
    75	The harness HTTP path sends lex+vec and enables rerank by default. If latency becomes a problem, tune the harness rather than falling back to subprocess `qmd query` on every turn.
    76	
    77	## Monitoring
    78	
    79	```sh
    80	qmd status
    81	qmd collection list
    82	qmd collection show pi-memory
    83	qmd context list
    84	qmd ls dream-memory | head
    85	qmd query "what did active-memory ship" -c pi-memory --json --explain -n 3
    86	curl -sf http://localhost:8181/health
    87	```
    88	
    89	Inside this repo:
    90	
    91	```sh
    92	pnpm dream doctor
    93	pnpm dream recall test "before_agent_start cache safety"
    94	pnpm dream recall last -n 10
    95	pnpm dream wiki reindex
    96	```
    97	
    98	## Editing collections
    99	
   100	Collection metadata:
   101	
   102	```sh
   103	qmd collection add <path> --name <name> --mask "**/*.md"
   104	qmd collection rename <old> <new>
   105	qmd collection remove <name>
   106	qmd collection include <name>
   107	qmd collection exclude <name>
   108	qmd collection update-cmd <name> 'git pull --ff-only'
   109	```
   110	
   111	Context metadata:
   112	
   113	```sh
   114	qmd context add qmd://<collection> "What this collection contains"
   115	qmd context add qmd://<collection>/<path> "What this subtree contains"
   116	qmd context rm qmd://<collection>/<path>
   117	```
   118	
   119	Files themselves are edited in their source folders. For `pi-memory`, use the `pi-memory` tools (`memory_write`, `memory_read`, `scratchpad`, `memory_search`) rather than editing live memory ad hoc. For `dream-memory`, canonical files under `profile/`, `project/`, and `tools/` should be written by the dream phase.
   120	
   121	## Hygiene rules
   122	
   123	- Keep `seed/` or benchmark corpora out of production recall. They can pollute top hits.
   124	- Prefer per-repo code collections over a single `~/Projects` collection.
   125	- Add path contexts generously; QMD returns context with results and it improves LLM selection.
   126	- Use `--chunk-strategy auto` for code collections so TS/JS/Python/Go/Rust chunk at function/class boundaries.
   127	- Active-memory should work from `pi-memory` alone; code collections and `dream-memory` are enrichment layers.

  qmd cleanup                   - Clear caches, vacuum DB

Query syntax (qmd query):
  QMD queries are either a single expand query (no prefix) or a multi-line
  document where every line is typed with lex:, vec:, or hyde:. This grammar
  matches the docs in docs/SYNTAX.md and is enforced in the CLI.

  Grammar:
    query          = expand_query | query_document ;
    expand_query   = text | explicit_expand ;
    explicit_expand= "expand:" text ;
    query_document = [ intent_line ] { typed_line } ;
    intent_line    = "intent:" text newline ;
    typed_line     = type ":" text newline ;
    type           = "lex" | "vec" | "hyde" ;
    text           = quoted_phrase | plain_text ;
    quoted_phrase  = '"' { character } '"' ;
    plain_text     = { character } ;
    newline        = "\n" ;

  Examples:
    qmd query "how does auth work"                # single-line → implicit expand
    qmd query $'lex: CAP theorem\nvec: consistency'  # typed query document
    qmd query $'lex: "exact matches" sports -baseball'  # phrase + negation lex search
    qmd query $'hyde: Hypothetical answer text'       # hyde-only document

  Constraints:
    - Standalone expand queries cannot mix with typed lines.
    - Query documents allow only lex:, vec:, or hyde: prefixes.
    - Each typed line must be single-line text with balanced quotes.

AI agents & integrations:
  - Run `qmd mcp` to expose the MCP server (stdio) to agents/IDEs.
  - Run `qmd skills get qmd --full` for version-matched agent instructions.
  - `qmd skill install` installs the QMD skill into ./.agents/skills/qmd.
  - Use `qmd skill install --global` for ~/.agents/skills/qmd.
  - `qmd --skill` is kept as an alias for `qmd skill show`.
  - Advanced: `qmd mcp --http ...` and `qmd mcp --http --daemon` are optional for custom transports.

Global options:

  QMD_EDITOR_URI             - Editor link template for clickable TTY search output

Search options:

  --all                      - Return all matches (pair with --min-score)
  --min-score <num>          - Minimum similarity score
  --full                     - Output full document instead of snippet
  -C, --candidate-limit <n>  - Max candidates to rerank (default 40, lower = faster)
  --no-rerank                - Skip LLM reranking (use RRF scores only, much faster on CPU)

  -l <num>                   - Maximum lines per file

# QMD - Query Markdown Documents

## How search works

QMD searches local markdown collections: notes, docs, wikis, transcripts, and
project knowledge bases. Use it before web search when the answer may already be
in indexed local files.

The workflow is always:

1. Search for candidate documents.
2. Retrieve the full source with `qmd get` or `qmd multi-get`.
3. Answer from retrieved text, citing paths or docids.

Do not answer from snippets alone when the user needs facts, decisions, quotes,
or nuance. Snippets are only leads.

Typical loop:

```bash
qmd search "merchant reality support interviews" -n 5
# leads: #abc123 concepts/customer-proximity.md; #def432 sources/merchant-call.md
qmd multi-get "#abc123,#def432" --format md
```

**Default to structured `qmd query` with `intent:`, `lex:`, `vec:`, and `hyde:`
fields that you write yourself.** You are a better query expander than the
built-in model: you know the user's actual goal, the domain vocabulary, and the
nearby-but-wrong concepts to avoid. Do not just paste the user's words into
`qmd query "..."` and hope the expansion model guesses right — supply the
`intent:` and craft the lexical and semantic terms deliberately (see
[Pick the right search mode](#pick-the-right-search-mode)).

When reporting what you retrieved, a compact note is enough; do not paste whole
files unless needed:

```text
Retrieved:
- #abc123 concepts/customer-proximity.md
- #def432 sources/merchant-call.md
```

## Pick the right search mode

Use **BM25 lexical search** when you know exact words, titles, names, code
symbols, or rare phrases:

```bash
qmd search "cockpit OKR Goodhart" -n 10
qmd search '"AI Before Headcount"' -c concepts -n 5
```

Use **`qmd query` with structured fields** when the user describes an idea
indirectly, uses different wording than the source, or needs conceptual recall.
**This is the default mode — write the fields yourself rather than leaning on
query expansion.** Combine exact anchors with semantic recall:

```bash
qmd query $'intent: Find the concept note about metrics as instruments without letting OKRs replace judgment.\nlex: cockpit instruments OKR Goodhart metrics judgment\nvec: data informed not metric driven product judgment\nhyde: A concept note says metrics are useful like cockpit instruments, but leaders should remain data-informed rather than metric-driven because OKRs and dashboards can Goodhart product judgment.'
```

Structured query fields (you author each one — do not delegate this to the
expansion model):

- `intent:` states what you are trying to find **and what to avoid**. Always
  supply this. It steers ranking away from nearby-but-wrong concepts.
- `lex:` exact terms, aliases, titles, code symbols, and rare words you expect
  in the source. This is your own keyword expansion.
- `vec:` paraphrases the idea in natural language, in source-like wording.
- `hyde:` describes the document or answer that would satisfy the request.

You do not need all four every time, but you should almost always write at least
`intent:` plus one of `lex:`/`vec:`. A bare `qmd query "the user's sentence"`
throws away the context only you have and relies on the built-in expander to
reconstruct it — prefer the structured form.

If you genuinely have nothing to expand (a single rare token, a verbatim phrase),
that is a job for `qmd search`, not bare `qmd query`:

```bash
qmd query --format json --explain $'intent: ...\nlex: ...\nvec: ...'  # inspect ranking
```

If `qmd query` is slow or model/GPU setup fails, fall back to `qmd search` with
better lexical terms.

## Retrieve sources

Search results include docids like `#abc123` and `qmd://...` paths. Fetch them:

```bash
qmd get "#abc123"
qmd get qmd://concepts/ai-before-headcount.md
qmd multi-get "#abc123,#def432" --format md
qmd multi-get 'concepts/{ai-before-headcount.md,data-informed-not-metric-driven.md}' --format md
qmd multi-get 'sources/podcast-2025-*.md' -l 80
```

Use `multi-get` when comparing several hits or gathering context across pages.

### Output is line-numbered and carries the docid — cite both

`get` and `multi-get` are **line-numbered by default** and always print the
document's `#docid` and `qmd://` path. So `get` output looks like:

```text
qmd://concepts/note.md  #abc123
---

1: # Metrics as instruments
2:
3: Treat dashboards like cockpit instruments...
```

Cite the docid and exact line numbers in your answer, and use the numbers to ask
for the next slice. Pass `--no-line-numbers` only when you need raw content to
copy verbatim (e.g. reproducing a code block).

When you need to open or edit the underlying file (e.g. hand a path to `Read`,
`Edit`, or an editor), add `--full-path`. It replaces the `qmd://` URL + docid
header with the document's on-disk path, falling back to the canonical header if
the file no longer exists on disk:

```text
$ qmd get "#abc123" --full-path
/Users/you/notes/concepts/note.md
---

1: # Metrics as instruments
```

`--full-path` works the same way on `qmd search` and `qmd query`: result paths
become the file's on-disk path — `./`-prefixed relative path when the file is
inside `$PWD`, absolute realpath otherwise — and the per-result `#docid` is
dropped because the path is the identifier. The leading `./` is intentional so
the output is unambiguously a filesystem path and cannot be mistaken for a bare
collection-relative string. Default search/query output still uses `qmd://`
URIs; only opt into `--full-path` when you specifically need a path you can hand
to a non-QMD tool.

### Read line ranges with the `:from:count` suffix — never pipe through `sed`/`head`/`tail`

`qmd get` slices files itself. Use the suffix or flags; do **not** shell out to
`sed -n`, `head`, `tail`, or `awk` to pull a line range. Piping defeats docid
resolution, virtual-path lookups, line numbering, and the header, and it is
slower and more error-prone.

The most compact form is a `:from:count` suffix right on the path or docid —
prefer it:

```bash
qmd get "#abc123:120:40"                  # 40 lines starting at line 120
qmd get qmd://concepts/note.md:200:60     # lines 200–259
qmd get "#abc123:120"                      # from line 120 to end of file
qmd get "#abc123" --from 120 -l 40         # equivalent, using flags
```

Suffix and flags:

- `<path>:<from>:<count>` — start at line `<from>`, read `<count>` lines. **Best
  for reading around a search hit.**
- `<path>:<from>` — start at `<from>`, read to end of file.
- `--from <line>` / `-l <lines>` — flag equivalents. Explicit flags override the
  suffix, so `... :5:2 -l 1` reads 1 line.
- `--no-line-numbers` — drop the `N:` prefixes (line numbers are on by default).

Wrong: `qmd get "#abc123" | sed -n '120,160p'`
Right: `qmd get "#abc123:120:40"`

Search results include a `:line` anchor on each hit — feed it straight into
`qmd get path:line:<n>` to read a window around the match (line numbers in the
output will start at `line`).

## Discover what is indexed

```bash
qmd collection list
qmd ls
qmd status
```

Add collection filters when broad searches drift into the wrong corpus:

```bash
qmd search "headcount autonomous agents" -c concepts -n 10
qmd query "merchant support product reality" -c concepts -c sources -n 10
```

Omit `-c` to search everything.

## MCP Tool: `query`

When using the MCP server, prefer structured searches:

```json
{
  "searches": [
    { "type": "lex", "query": "cockpit OKR Goodhart" },
    { "type": "vec", "query": "data informed not metric driven product judgment" },
    { "type": "hyde", "query": "A concept note explains that metrics are useful as instruments, but leaders should not let OKRs or dashboards replace judgment." }
  ],
  "intent": "Find the concept note about using metrics as instruments without becoming metric-driven.",
  "collections": ["concepts"],
  "limit": 10
}
```

Query types:

- `lex` — BM25 keyword search. Best for exact terms, names, titles, and code.
- `vec` — vector semantic search. Best for natural-language concepts.
- `hyde` — vector search using a hypothetical answer/document passage.

## Query craft

Good QMD searches mix three things:

1. **Title/alias anchors:** exact page titles, named entities, phrases.
2. **Semantic paraphrase:** how a human would describe the idea.
3. **Negative space:** enough intent to avoid nearby-but-wrong concepts.

Examples:

```bash
# Exact-ish title lookup
qmd search '"arm the rebels" merchants tools big companies' -c concepts

# Semantic concept lookup
qmd query $'intent: Find the customer proximity concept, not generic customer delight.\nlex: support pseudonymous merchant customer interviews\nvec: founder stays close to merchant reality through support and product use'

# Source lookup
qmd search "six-week cadence WhatsApp merchant relationships Shawn Ryan" -c sources -n 10
```

## Setup and maintenance

Only mutate indexes when the user asked for setup or maintenance. Searching and
retrieving are safe; collection/index mutation is not a casual first step.

```bash
npm install -g @tobilu/qmd
qmd collection add ~/notes --name notes
qmd update
qmd embed
```

Health and diagnostics:

```bash
qmd doctor
qmd status
qmd pull
```

`qmd doctor` checks config, model cache, device/GPU setup, vector fingerprints,
and common environment overrides. If a model-backed command fails, run it before
changing configuration.

## MCP setup

See `references/mcp-setup.md` for Claude Code, Claude Desktop, OpenClaw, and HTTP
server configuration.

## Pitfalls

- **Do not stop at snippets.** Fetch documents before making claims.
- **Do not slice files with `sed`/`head`/`tail`.** Use the `path:from:count`
  suffix (e.g. `qmd get "#abc123:120:40"`) or `--from`/`-l`. Output is already
  line-numbered; piping breaks docid resolution, the header, and virtual paths.
- **Do not lean on query expansion.** Write `intent:`/`lex:`/`vec:`/`hyde:`
  yourself. A bare `qmd query "user sentence"` discards the context only you
  have. You expand the query; the model just ranks.
- **Do not overuse semantic search.** If you know exact titles or terms, BM25 is
  faster and often better.
- **Do not mutate indexes casually.** `qmd collection add`, `qmd update`, and
  `qmd embed` change local state and can be expensive.
- **Model-backed commands can be environment-sensitive.** If `qmd query`,
  `qmd vsearch`, or reranking fails because local models/GPU are unavailable,
  use `qmd search` and stronger lexical/structured terms.
- **Ambiguous user wording needs intent.** Add `intent:` rather than hoping query
  expansion guesses the right domain.
- **Collection names matter.** Search `concepts` for synthesized wiki pages,
  `sources` for transcripts/raw source pages, and docs collections for code or
  project documentation.

# QMD MCP Server Setup

## Install

```bash
npm install -g @tobilu/qmd
qmd collection add ~/path/to/markdown --name myknowledge
qmd embed
```

## Configure MCP Client

**Claude Code** (`~/.claude/settings.json`):
```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "qmd": { "command": "qmd", "args": ["mcp"] }
  }
}
```

**Claude Desktop** (`~/Library/Application Support/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json`):
```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "qmd": { "command": "qmd", "args": ["mcp"] }
  }
}
```

**OpenClaw** (`~/.openclaw/openclaw.json`):
```json
{
  "mcp": {
    "servers": {
      "qmd": { "command": "qmd", "args": ["mcp"] }
    }
  }
}
```

## HTTP Mode

```bash
qmd mcp --http              # Port 8181
qmd mcp --http --daemon     # Background
qmd mcp stop                # Stop daemon
```

## Tools

### structured_search

Search with pre-expanded queries.

```json
{
  "searches": [
    { "type": "lex", "query": "keyword phrases" },
    { "type": "vec", "query": "natural language question" },
    { "type": "hyde", "query": "hypothetical answer passage..." }
  ],
  "limit": 10,
  "collection": "optional",
  "minScore": 0.0
}
```

| Type | Method | Input |
|------|--------|-------|
| `lex` | BM25 | Keywords (2-5 terms) |
| `vec` | Vector | Question |
| `hyde` | Vector | Answer passage (50-100 words) |

### get

Retrieve document by path or `#docid`.

| Param | Type | Description |
|-------|------|-------------|
| `path` | string | File path or `#docid` |
| `full` | bool? | Return full content |
| `lineNumbers` | bool? | Add line numbers |

### multi_get

Retrieve multiple documents.

| Param | Type | Description |
|-------|------|-------------|
| `pattern` | string | Glob or comma-separated list |
| `maxBytes` | number? | Skip large files (default 10KB) |

### status

Index health and collections. No params.

## Troubleshooting

- **Not starting**: `which qmd`, `qmd mcp` manually
- **No results**: `qmd collection list`, `qmd embed`
- **Slow first search**: Normal, models loading (~3GB)

# How I Work

Bias: caution over speed; for trivial tasks use judgment.

## Think Before Coding
- State assumptions explicitly; uncertain → ask. Multiple interpretations → present them, don't pick silently.
- Simpler approach exists → say so; push back when warranted. Confused → stop, name it, ask.

## Simplicity First
- Minimum code that solves the problem; nothing speculative: no features beyond the ask, no abstractions for single-use code, no unrequested configurability, no error handling for impossible scenarios.
- 200 lines that could be 50 → rewrite. Test: would a senior engineer call this overcomplicated?

## Surgical Changes
- Before adding behavior, trace the owning entrypoint/call chain and find the existing specialized code; prefer reusing/refactoring/removing over adding parallel logic. Reuse existing types/utilities/patterns before writing new ones; don't broaden public APIs unless required.
- Don't improve adjacent code/comments/formatting; match existing style. Unrelated dead code → mention, don't delete.
- Quality blocking the task → improve it as part of the change, call it out. Real issue outside the task → flag, don't expand scope.
- Remove orphans YOUR change created; leave pre-existing ones. Every changed line traces to the request.

## Goal-Driven Execution
- Verifiable goals: "fix the bug" → "test that reproduces it, make it pass". Multi-step → brief plan, one verify per step.
- Spec work: slices traceable to spec/issue; "what's left?" = concrete file/task deltas; checkpoint before risky refactors.
- Don't fight errors: same error twice → stop, gather evidence (local docs/source first, then web) before the next fix.

## Earned Progression
- Ambition names the desired state; motivation supplies energy; proof earns trust. Keep them separate.
- Progress by earning confidence: define the vision, prove the current step, then automate/delegate only what the proof can vouch for.
- Confidence comes from evidence: tests, gates, types, monitoring, data checks, runbooks, reviews, and observed outcomes.
- Every escape teaches the system: log what slipped, name the missing signal, add the smallest gate/monitor/process that catches it next time.

     5	
     6	## Context
     7	
     8	ADR 0009 Amendment 1 fixed the recall *ranking* model (decay-weight, not hard-filter) and declared **ACL — `sensitivity`/`visibility` — the only hard gate, run before scoring.** It did not specify *where* that gate executes. The working assumption (carried into the Slice 2 plan) was a frontmatter exclusion: parse each candidate's `visibility`/`sensitivity` and drop the ones the session may not see.
     9	
    10	Two findings (Luke + verification, 2026-06-23) kill that assumption:
    11	
    12	1. **The ACL frontmatter fields are dead.** `visibility` and `sensitivity` are defined, defaulted by `defaultCaptureVisibility()`, and written — but consumed by **zero** read paths (audit: `visibility` 3 refs, `sensitivity` 3 refs, all the definition itself; vs `status` 85, `scope` 29). The in-band ACL was never wired.
    13	
    14	2. **The recall backend has no metadata/path filter — the collection is its only partition primitive.** `qmd query --help` exposes exactly one scoping flag: `-c, --collection <name>` ("filter by one or more collections"). The query grammar is `lex:`/`vec:`/`hyde:` only — no frontmatter predicate, no subdir-within-collection filter. The harness's HTTP `/query` body sends `{ searches, collections, limit, rerank }`; `collections` is the *only* scoping field. A collection is a named indexed folder (`qmd collection add <path> --name --mask`). `--index <name>` offers a harder, fully separate index tier.
    15	
    16	So a frontmatter ACL was not merely "not robust" (Luke's instinct) — it was **unenforceable at query time** on this backend, and is also in-band (mutable by the same LLM that authors memory) and fail-open (a missing/edited flag leaks). The robust pattern used by every production memory system is the inverse: the scope key *is the storage address*, enforced by the store — mem0 `user_id`/`agent_id`/`app_id` partitions, Zep/Graphiti mandatory `group_id` namespacing, LangMem namespace tuples, Letta agent-scoped blocks. None enforce isolation from document content.
    17	
    18	The harness already federates over `collections: string[]` (`searchMemoryHttp`, `activeRecallCollections()`), and the canonical store already lays files under a global root (`~/.agents/memory/{shared,harness/<id>,episodic,inbox}`) and per-project roots (`~/.agents/projects/<sanitize(gitRoot)>/memory/{…}`) — the layout locked in ADR 0007 D1 (`canonical/paths.ts`). The enforcement mechanism is therefore mostly already built; this ADR commits to using it as the gate and trims the now-redundant frontmatter.
    19	
    20	## Decision
    21	
    22	1. **Scope & visibility are enforced by physical partition = qmd collection. The session read-set is the list of collections passed to `collections`; nothing outside it is reachable.** Two recall collections, one per root (granularity resolved 2026-06-23):
    23	   - `canonical-global` ← `~/.agents/memory/` (masks `shared/**` + `harness/<id>/**`) — the always-in-read-set partition.
    24	   - `canonical-project-<slug>` ← `~/.agents/projects/<slug>/memory/` (same mask), where `<slug> = sanitize(gitRoot)` — Claude Code's convention, reused verbatim via `agentsMemoryRoot`.
    25	
    26	   `inbox/` (raw pre-consolidation) and `episodic/` (chronicle) are **not** indexed into the recall collections. `harness/<id>/` is *bundled into* its root's collection rather than split out: the harness id is provenance, not an ACL boundary (all harnesses are the same user), so cross-harness recall is a feature of the unified store, and harness-relevance is a soft ranking weight (via `provenance.origin`), never a hard partition. The hard boundary is **project isolation** (a `work-X` record never reaches a personal-repo session) and global-vs-project — both captured by per-root collections. Enforcement is the federation list, not a post-fetch filter. **Fail-closed by construction:** an empty read-set yields zero results — qmd only searches the named collections.
    27	
    28	2. **Global/shared memory is the `canonical-global` collection, a member of *every* session's read-set.** This is how a fact recalls across all profiles/users/projects: the consolidation writer places it in the global root (`~/.agents/memory/shared/` for cross-harness facts, `harness/<id>/` for harness-specific), it indexes into `canonical-global`, and every session federates over `canonical-global` regardless of which project it runs in. No per-record "shared" flag — placement is the declaration, the always-included collection is the mechanism. (Mirrors mem0 `app_id` defaults, LangMem shared namespace, Letta shared blocks, Zep shared `group_id`.)
    29

    43

The *path* is the source of truth the enforcement layer reads. Frontmatter never gates recall; it documents and (for `secret`) influences placement. This keeps the gate out of reach of the authoring LLM.
    45	
    46	6. **The read-set is resolved once per session and is span-stable (ADR 0008).** Session entitlements (`canonical-project-<current-slug>` plus always-on `canonical-global`) are computed at session start and held constant across the cache span.     47	
    48	7. **A project's collection is auto-registered on first canonical write (resolved 2026-06-23).** The consolidation writer registers (`qmd collection add`) and embeds the project's collection the moment it writes the first canonical record into a new project root — no manual step, no setup command, and the collection exists exactly when there is content to index.     50	8. **GC reindex is eventual, via the next dream pass (resolved 2026-06-23).** Post-migration GC (ADR 0009 Amendment 1 pt 4) only *deletes* superseded files; it does not reindex. The next scheduled dream consolidation already runs `qmd update` → `qmd embed` (`dream.ts:109`), which prunes the deleted docs. **Requirement:** because a recall between a GC sweep and the next dream may return a hit whose file is gone, the recall path must tolerate a transiently-missing document (degrade/skip, never crash) — a Slice 2 build gate.
    51	
    52	## Alternatives Considered
    53	
    54	| Alternative | Rejected because |
    55	|---|---|
    56	| Frontmatter `visibility`/`sensitivity` exclusion at recall (the Slice 2 working plan) | Unenforceable — qmd has no metadata filter. Also in-band (the authoring LLM can edit the flag), fail-open (missing/malformed → leaks), and requires every reader to cooperate. Contradicts ADR 0009's "hard gate." |
    57	| Single `canonical` collection + filter by subdirectory at query time | No qmd primitive: query grammar is lex/vec/hyde, the only filter is `-c collection`. There is no path/prefix predicate to enforce. |
    58	| Per-record "shared" flag for cross-profile recall | Same in-band/fail-open weakness. Placement in the always-included `canonical-profile` collection achieves it without a flag. |
    59	| Separate `qmd --index` per scope (hard isolation everywhere) | Heavier than needed for project/tool scopes (separate DBs, separate embed cycles). Reserved for `secret` only, where the stronger guarantee is worth the cost. |
    60	| Keep `scope` in frontmatter *and* derive collection from path | Two sources of truth for the same fact drift. Path is authoritative because it is what qmd indexes; the frontmatter copy is redundant bytes. |
    61	
    62	## Trade-offs / Consequences
    63	
    64	- **Collection lifecycle becomes a first-class step.** A new project means `qmd collection add` + `qmd embed` before its memory is reachable — resolved as auto-register on first canonical write (Decision 7). Embed cost scales with the number of active project collections.
    65	- **The collection is the finest ACL granularity.** Two records needing different visibility must live in different directories — which holds by construction once scope = path. No intra-directory visibility splits.
    66	- **Schema change ripples into the gated migration.** `canonical/frontmatter.ts`, `canonical/serialize.ts`, and the P2 migration writer drop `scope`/`visibility`/`origin` and add `provenance.device_id`. The migration apply is still gated on Luke's full-ledger sign-off (unchanged); this only changes the shape it writes.
    67	- **Slice 2 is re-scoped:** the ACL hard-gate is "compute the session read-set of collection names + pass them to `searchMemoryHttp({ collections })`, fail-closed", *not* a frontmatter parser. Most of the federation plumbing (`activeRecallCollections`, multi-collection `/query`) already exists.
    68	- **`status`/`confidence` weighting (ADR 0009 Amendment 1) is unaffected** — it runs *after* the read-set narrows candidates, exactly as the amendment specifies (ACL narrows first, then weight).
    69	
    70	## Resolved (2026-06-23, by grill)
    71	
    72	- **Granularity** → per-root, two recall collections (Decision 1). Project isolation is the hard boundary; the harness split is soft (provenance + ranking weight).
    73	- **Registration** → auto on first canonical write (Decision 7).
    74	- **Secret tier** → separate `qmd --index`, not a quarantine collection (Decision 3) — strongest isolation, at the cost of index-targeting plumbing.
    75	- **GC ↔ reindex** → eventual, via the next dream's `qmd update` + `embed` (Decision 8); recall must tolerate a transiently-missing doc.
    76	
    77	## Open / Slice 2 build tasks
    78	
    79	- The `paths.ts` comment "`scope` frontmatter records global-vs-project so a misfiled note stays classifiable" is **superseded** — scope is now path-derived (the directory *is* the decision; there is no independent intended-scope to misfile against). Update that comment when the schema trim lands.
    80	- Index-targeting plumbing for the secret index (daemon `index` param or a second daemon) — does not exist today (`store.ts` recall path passes only `collections`).
    81	- Recall-path tolerance for a GC-deleted-but-still-indexed doc (degrade/skip).
    82	- `<slug>` collision: handled by Claude Code's `sanitize(gitRoot)`, reused verbatim — no new convention needed.

Per-store consolidators on divergent corpora is the named industry anti-pattern (definition drift, irreconcilable conflicts).
     9	
    10	Two forcing functions converged. (1) The requirement that **CC/Codex learnings be *actively recalled* like Pi's**, not merely injected once at session start. (2) The 2026-06-10 disposition in `memory-architecture.md` set an A/B deadline (2026-06-30 / 30 sessions) to *choose the primary memory path*. This ADR resolves that deadline.
    11	
    12	The unification target is not greenfield: `extensions/dream-memory/src/lib/agents-path.ts` already defines `~/.agents/projects/<git-root>/memory/` as "the write target for agentic dream mode," `dream/agentic.ts` already writes there, and `claudeMemoryRoot()` already reads CC's native dir as a read-only source. The decision below builds on it, so requalification is a blocking precondition (Consequences), not an assumption.
    13	
    14	## Decision
    15	
    16	1. **Canonical store = two namespaced roots** (layout locked 2026-06-22, superseding the earlier flat-`~/.agents/memory` sketch — the per-project root matches the existing agentic-dream write target `~/.agents/projects/<slug>/memory/` and CC's `~/.claude/projects/<slug>/`):
    17	   - **Global / cross-project:** `~/.agents/memory/` — `shared/` + `harness/{pi,claude-code,codex}/` + `episodic/` + `inbox/`.
    18	   - **Per-project:** `~/.agents/projects/<sanitize(gitRoot)>/memory/` — same `shared/` + `harness/*` + `episodic/` + `inbox/` namespacing inside.
    19	
    20	   Profile/global facts live in the global root; repo-scoped facts under the matching project root (`scope` frontmatter still records the distinction, so a misfiled note stays classifiable). Canonical harness IDs `pi`/`claude-code`/`codex`, no aliases. Obsidian demotes to an optional **read-only view** (the vault symlinks both roots), never load-bearing.
    21	
    22	2. **Three write classes, not one writer (resolves the "single writer" ambiguity).** The store has exactly three mutation authorities, each scoped:
    23	   - **Raw capture writers** (any harness, any harvester) may append *only* into `inbox/` as immutable events. Pi included — Pi does **not** write canonical records directly; it appends to `inbox/` like every other source.
    24	   - **Canonical consolidated writer = one** dream-bridge consolidation process, holding a global store lock (see ADR 0008 + spec P3). It is the *only* mutator of `shared/`, `harness/*`, `episodic/`.
    25	   - **Model-facing injectors = one per harness** (CC native, Codex native, `pi-memory` `profile-base.ts`). "Single writer" was always about the canonical *store*, never injection. This preserves the 2026-06-10 rule that `pi-memory` — not dream-memory — owns Pi profile-core injection. For Pi the bridge may *compute* recall candidates but **must not inject**; a single-owner injection guard enforces it (spec P4).
    26	
    27	3. **Build on the own stack; do not adopt Mem0/Letta as runtime.** Every component an external memory system sells already exists in the bridge, tuned to constraints they do not model (cache byte-stability per ADR 0008, human-gated dreaming, three-harness normalisation, structured patch edits). Borrow *algorithms* (the conflict-merge verbs are already mirrored in `dream/patch-schema.ts`), never the dependency. This is the primary-path choice the 2026-06-10 deadline asked for.
    28	
    29	4. **Fold natives by capture + harvest, not by disabling.** CC `autoMemory` and Codex `memories` (+ chronicle) stay **ON as capture surfaces**: they capture and self-inject their own subset; the bridge **harvests their dirs read-only** into `inbox/` via the dream/patch pipeline, provenance-tagged. The bridge **never writes back into native dirs** (keeps single-writer intact). Keeping Codex `memories=true` preserves chronicle's screen-memory injection. `pi-memory`'s write/extraction repoints to the canonical **inbox** (append-only); consolidation promotes — its Pi-core injection role stays.
    30	   - **Harvested native memory is untrusted external input.** It lands in `inbox/quarantine/<origin>/`, **not** `shared/`. Promotion to `shared/` or `harness/*` requires the consolidation pass to classify it (scope + sensitivity). A native self-injected fact that canonical has since *corrected* must not silently win: when canonical contradicts a still-surfacing native fact, the bridge injects an explicit appended correction rather than relying on dedup to suppress it (see Decision 5).
    31	
    32	5. **Recall = global minus self, namespaced — tail only.** The bridge's injected recall for harness X = canonical memory **minus what X already self-injects**, scoped to `shared ∪ harness/X`. Two hard constraints:
    33	   - **Tail-recall only.** "Global minus self" depends on volatile per-session state (native dirs, qmd index, similarity scores) and therefore **must never influence cached-core bytes** — it touches only the volatile trailing region (ADR 0008). Core dedup is manifest/snapshot-based, never embedding-based.
    34	   - **Embedding similarity is a candidate signal, never a deletion authority.** Suppression of a candidate requires an exact source ID, an exact normalised-text hash, or an entailment check — because corrections, negations, dates, numbers, and scope changes sit *embedding-near* the stale fact they replace. A candidate carrying correction/negation/date/number/repo/tool/scope language defaults to **injected**. Visibility (not origin) decides cross-harness surfacing — see Decision 7.
    35	
    36	6. **Shadows = offline-bench backends only.** `letta-shadow`/`mem0-shadow` register nothing live and are evaluated by snapshot-replay (`scripts/bench/`), not live traffic. Move them out of the daily-driver profile; re-bench against the new canonical corpus post-migration. The build-vs-buy *decision* (don't adopt) rests on grounds the benchmark cannot measure — human-gated dreaming, the cache contract external systems don't model, the already-tuned three-harness pipeline — **not** on snapshot-replay overlap, which is circular (it scores retrieval on a corpus already shaped by the own stack). The benchmark is a smoke test plus falsification harness (spec P6), not the justification.
    37

New harvested/captured facts (incl. chronicle screen summaries) default to **origin-private**, promoted to broader visibility only by a classification pass. This is what stops a Codex-captured client token surfacing as Pi or CC context.
    39	
    40	8. **The backlink graph is built in — explicit edges, not embeddings.** The QMD pivot dropped basic-memory's `## Relations` section (`dream.ts` `stripBasicMemorySections`) on the theory that embeddings answer "what's related." They don't: embedding similarity is undirected, untyped, and non-deterministic, so it cannot carry `supersedes` corrections, `links` provenance, or a graph a human can audit. Canonical records therefore carry **explicit outbound edges** — inline `[[permalink]]` links (Obsidian renders the backlink graph for free) plus `links`/`relates` frontmatter — and the serialiser **converts relations instead of dropping them** (`convertRelationsToLinks`, strip-and-keep). No separate graph store and no qmd change: the graph is a pure function over the note set (`buildBacklinkIndex`), and qmd similarity stays the *fuzzy* recall signal alongside the *deterministic* edge set. Dedup/consolidation (Decision 5) may use edges as a hard signal (`supersedes`, exact `links`) but still never uses similarity as a deletion authority.
    41	
    42	## Alternatives Considered
    43	
    44	| Alternative | Rejected because |
    45	|---|---|
    46	| Per-harness stores + a reconciler pass | The named anti-pattern; divergent corpora already proved drift (disjoint 124/81 sets). |
    47	| Adopt Mem0/Letta as the runtime | Regresses human-gated dreaming (ahead of the commercial pack), discards the bridge's tuned pipeline, and retrofits constraints they don't model. Kept only as offline benchmarks. |
    48	| Disable CC + Codex native memory; bridge owns all capture | Simplest, but loses CC's extractor (whose memories Luke wants surfaced) and — because Codex's memory switch gates chronicle — kills chronicle's screen-memory injection. |
    49	| Symlink native dirs at the canonical store | Format pollution (CC owns its file shape) + two writers on one dir; breaks single-writer. |
    50	| Make the bridge the single *injector* too | Violates the 2026-06-10 cache-governance decision; `pi-memory`'s `profile-base` is the proven cache-safe Pi core renderer. |
    51	
    52	## Consequences
    53	
    54	- Implementation is a grouped program — see `docs/specs/cross-harness-memory-unification-spec.md` (canonical skeleton, one-off migration, harvest watchers, dedup-on-inject, qmd re-point, `pi-memory` write repoint, shadow relocation, cutover).
    55	- The mutation/cache behaviour of the unified store is governed by **ADR 0008** (two-region contract).
    56	- This **supersedes the 2026-06-30 A/B "choose primary path" deadline**: primary = own unified stack; shadows retained only as offline benchmarks with the existing metric set (cache-base churn, recall precision/usefulness, correction rate, duplicate/stale rate, tool overhead, prompt bytes).
    57	- One-off migration must union pi + obsidian as full members and ingest CC/Codex (chronicle → episodic) as read-only sources, deduped in a single pass, via dry-run → quarantine review → apply. **File-count reconciliation is not a data-loss gate** — migration runs on a **claim-level ledger** (atomic claims, source hashes/spans, content-addressed IDs, transactional apply + rollback, ledger-driven idempotent rerun). Spec P2.
    58	- **Blocking preconditions** (decisions are accepted; these must close before migration applies — spec P0.5/P1): (a) dream-bridge code is *requalified* as live, not the retired/dead path `memory-architecture.md` describes; (b) Pi compaction-event availability and Pi write-path ownership are resolved (they determine cache safety and the single-writer claim); (c) `recall-routing.ts` is updated for canonical collections **before** the qmd cutover; (d) a canonical store write-lock + atomic-write/WAL protocol exists before any concurrent harvester runs.

     1	# ADR 0008: Memory cache-stability contract (two regions, frozen-per-span)
     2	
     3	**Status:** Proposed (2026-06-22) — contract locked; moves to Accepted once the versioned-snapshot byte-stability gate (spec P5) and the Pi compaction-hook question (P0.5) are proven.
     4	**Related:** ADR 0007, `docs/cache-strategy.md`, `~/.pi/agent/skills/pi-cache-stability/SKILL.md`, the cache golden rule in `pi-dev.md`
     5	
     6	## Context
     7	
     8	ADR 0007 makes one canonical store serve active recall across Pi, Claude Code, and Codex. Active recall "like Pi's" is a per-turn read, which collides directly with the cache golden rule: `params.system` and `tools[]` must stay byte-stable across same-cwd sessions, and dynamic data must live in appended messages, never in the cached prefix.
     9	
    10	The unresolved question was: when a memory is **modified or removed**, how does that propagate without busting each harness's prompt-prefix cache mid-session? The three harnesses already share the same physics — a stable core is read **once at session start** and injected into the cached prefix (CC `MEMORY.md`, Codex Developer Message, Pi's `profile-base` snapshot), while dynamic recall is **appended per turn** (Pi's `active-memory` tail). The contract below formalises that shape and makes the mutation policy explicit so future memory work cannot silently violate it.
    11	
    12	## Decision
    13	
    14	Two regions, enforced per harness:
    15	
    16	- **Core** — small, slow-changing, deterministically injected into the harness's cached prefix at **SessionStart**, then **frozen for the cached span**. Critically, **core renders from a versioned, explicitly-promoted snapshot — not a live read of canonical memory.** The renderer reads only `core-snapshots/<harness>/<scope>/<base_epoch>.md` plus a stable manifest. Harvest, qmd state, dedup decisions, tombstones, similarity scores, and native-memory churn change *only the trailing recall* until consolidation **promotes a new base epoch**. Without this, two same-cwd sessions straddling a harvest would re-render different core bytes and re-bill the whole prefix every session — defeating the cache win even though the change happened "at a boundary." Boundaries (SessionStart, compaction) re-*render* the current epoch; only an epoch bump *changes* it.
    17	- **Recall** — volatile, trailing, per-turn, **never cached**.
    18	
    19	Mutability classes (which region a fact may enter):
    20	
    21	- **Core admits only durable, low-volatility, low-harm facts** — identity, stable preferences. **Corrections, removals, security rules, credentials, project state, tool choices, and "do not do X" facts are barred from core** and live in recall, because a stale one frozen in the prefix cannot be unsent. Corrections carry supersession metadata (`supersedes`, `valid_from`, `valid_until`, `scope`, `confidence`).
    22	- A **critical-revocation** tail block is appended every turn (high priority) for facts that *must* override a possibly-stale core line; for the highest-severity revocations the harness may force a new session / base epoch rather than wait for a boundary.
    23	
    24	Mutation policy:
    25	
    26	- **Mutations never touch a live session's core.** A write/merge/remove lands in `~/.agents/memory`; it surfaces mid-session only via the volatile recall region, and reaches core only when the next promoted base epoch is rendered at *that harness's* next boundary.
    27	- **Removal = soft-invalidate** (tombstone + decay via `decay-prune.ts`); physical prune happens only at consolidation, so cached prefix bytes never shift under a running session. **Tombstones are first-class in retrieval** — qmd must exclude or filter tombstoned records *before* ranking, so a deleted fact never reaches recall even before physical prune, and a correction outranks its tombstoned predecessor.
    28	- **Cache domains are per-harness.** Sharing the store ≠ sharing prefix bytes. Each harness renders its own core; a base-epoch bump pays the cache cost only on *its* next boundary — never mid-session, never cross-harness.
    29	
    30	`pi-memory`'s `profile-base` snapshot is Pi's proven cache-safe core renderer; the bridge's `active-memory` tail is the volatile recall. The same split is required of CC and Codex rendering.
    31	
    32	## Alternatives Considered
    33	
    34	| Alternative | Rejected because |
    35	|---|---|
    36	| All memory in the trailing region (no cached core) | Zero cache-bust risk, but forfeits the prefix-cache cost win (41–80% on stable prefixes) and re-bills stable facts every turn. |
    37	| Re-render the core every turn | Busts the prefix cache on every turn — the exact failure the golden rule exists to prevent. |
    38	| Immediate physical delete of a removed memory mid-session | Shifts cached prefix bytes under a live session. Soft-invalidate + deferred prune avoids it. |
    39	| Render core live from canonical memory at each boundary | Harvest/consolidation churns canonical constantly, so two same-cwd sessions render different core bytes and re-bill the prefix every session. Versioned promoted snapshot (epoch bump only at consolidation) bounds churn. |
    40	| Freeze the core for the whole session, never re-render | Misses corrected/removed facts for the life of a long session; compaction is a free re-render point already being paid for. |
    41	
    42	## Consequences
    43	
    44	- The bridge gains a **compaction subscription** to re-render the core: CC exposes `PreCompact`; **Pi exposes `session_before_compact` + `session_compact` to extensions** (verified P0.5 — `agent-session.ts:2594-2676`, `docs/extensions.md`/`compaction.md`); Codex exposes none and **gracefully degrades to SessionStart-only** refresh. **No `pi-mono-fork` patch is required** — the Pi seam already exists. (The CC side does need a `PreCompact` hook wired into `harness-cli.ts`, which today handles no compaction event.)
    45	- **Accepted tension:** a stale-but-durable core fact can persist in a long-running session's *frozen core* until its next boundary; the volatile recall *adds* a correction alongside it but cannot *unsend* the stale prefix line. This is acceptable **only because the mutability classes bar high-harm/mutable facts from core in the first place** — compaction does **not** reliably bound staleness (it is non-deterministic, may not fire before the harmful action, and Codex likely has none), so the design must not depend on it. The critical-revocation tail block, not compaction, is the safety mechanism for anything dangerous.
    46	- All future memory work must honour this contract; the `pi-cache-stability` skill checklist is the enforcement point and links here.

    27	5. **Superseded = down-weighted, not filtered (amended 2026-06-23 — see Amendment 1).** A `superseded` record stays on disk and stays **reachable by recall**, but ranks low. Two read surfaces, two rules:
    28	   - **Always-loaded index** (Tier 1, `MEMORY.md`): renders **active records only**, scope-gated — current truth in the cached-core budget, nothing stale. This is a *render* budget choice, not a reachability gate.
    29	   - **Per-turn recall** (Tier 2, semantic retrieval): scores **every record except those an ACL blocks**, by `score = semantic_similarity × decay(age, last_used) × statusWeight × confidenceWeight`. A superseded record is reachable at low weight (`statusWeight ≈ 0.3` vs active `1.0`), so a query that *only* matches the old truth can still surface it; a query that matches both surfaces the current one first. The existing freshness caveat (`<system-reminder>` appended for records older than ~1 day, `recall-selection.ts`) makes surfacing a superseded record safe — the model is told it may be stale.
    30	   - **ACL is the only hard gate.** `sensitivity`/`visibility` exclusions run *before* scoring (a security/privacy invariant, not a relevance call); `status`/`confidence`/`age` only *weight*, never exclude. Rationale (Luke, 2026-06-22): a hard `status:active` filter makes a record unreachable — "how would recall know about other artifacts if they're not visible?" — destroying the audit-trail/reversibility value of keeping it on disk. Temporal decay already solves "old truth ranks below new truth" without hiding anything.
    31	
    32	   **Deletion is allowed, but only as post-migration GC (amended 2026-06-23 — see Amendment 1).** Superseded records *are* deletable — Luke is fine deleting replaced facts. But deletion is a separate, explicitly human-triggered **GC** step that removes records superseded longer than a grace window (N days since `superseded_at`); it is **never part of `reconcile` and never runs during the migration**. The migration retains all 29 superseded records (the approved lossless diff is unchanged) because the one-shot LLM judge is least proven exactly there — retention keeps it reversible. GC reclaims them later, once the judge has a track record, when a wrong supersede call is cheap to catch and re-add.
    33	
    34	6. **Propose, then gate.** The judge only *proposes*. For migration, the full reconciled ledger (merges + supersedes + scope assignments) is presented for Luke's sign-off before any apply (P2 decision). For ingestion, `reconcileOne` slots into the existing human-gated dream consolidation — it adds no always-on automation. (ADR 0007: human-gated dreaming is a kept advantage.)
    35	
    36	7. **Filter scaffolding before reconcile.** Codex episodic boilerplate (the three repeating template section types, ~1,050 fragments) and oversized claims (e.g. the 446 KB blob) are quarantined *before* embedding/judging: they are scaffolding, not facts, and would waste judge calls and pollute clusters. They remain in the ledger as explicit quarantine, never dropped.
    37	
    38	## Alternatives Considered
    39	
    40	| Alternative | Rejected because |
    41	|---|---|
    42	| mem0-style in-place `ADD / UPDATE / DELETE / NOOP` | Hard-delete is unrecoverable under a fallible LLM judge, discards provenance, and violates ADR 0007 D5 ("never a deletion authority"). |
    43	| Migration-only reconciler (throwaway) | Ingestion needs the identical detect-resolve; two implementations drift — the per-store-consolidator anti-pattern ADR 0007 rejects, in miniature. |
    44	| Render superseded records in the always-loaded index | Pollutes the cached-core budget with stale truth. The index renders active-only — but the record stays *reachable via per-turn recall* (down-weighted), so this is a render choice, not a reachability gate. |
    45	| Hard-filter `status:active` at recall (original Decision 5) | Makes superseded records unreachable, defeating the audit-trail/reversibility reason to keep them on disk; a query matching only the old phrasing finds nothing. Temporal decay-weighting ranks current truth above stale without hiding either. Amended 2026-06-23. |
    46	| Embedding cosine as the merge/supersede authority | ADR 0007 D5: corrections, negations, dates, numbers, and scope changes sit *embedding-near* the fact they replace; similarity cannot carry `supersedes`. |
    47	| Add an external embedding/memory dependency | The local MLX `embedBatch` already runs (ADR 0007 D3 build-on-own-stack); a new dep adds cost and a singleton-dep footgun for zero gain. |
    48	| Share the reconciler with the per-turn recall path too | Recall-time suppression must stay exact/manifest-based to protect cached-core bytes (ADR 0007 D5/ADR 0008); only the *writer* path may use embedding+judge. |
    49	
    50	## Consequences
    51	
    52	- New module `extensions/dream-memory/src/reconcile/` (not under `migration/`, because it is not migration-specific): an `Embedder` seam over `embedBatch`, a `judge()` over `callPiModel`, `reconcileBulk`/`reconcileOne`, and Zod `Decision`/`MergeProposal` schemas. P2b (#382) builds it and wires the migration caller; a later spec phase wires the dream-consolidation caller.
    53	- Canonical frontmatter (`canonical/frontmatter.ts`) gains additive fields: `status: active | superseded` (default `active`), `superseded_by`, and `provenance: claim_id[]`.
    54	- Active recall ranking (`active-memory/recall-selection.ts`, `decay.ts`) extends the decay weight to factor `status` and `confidence`, never filtering on them; only ACL (`sensitivity`/`visibility`) hard-gates, ahead of scoring. The always-loaded index render (`harness-cli.ts` SessionStart) stays active-only and scope-gated.
    55	- Index/snapshot re-render is **scope-gated by the consolidation watermark**: a scope's `MEMORY.md`/core-snapshot epoch bumps only when that scope's event watermark advances (`dream.ts` already gates consolidation this way), so dormant projects are never re-rendered — no token spend re-revising memory nothing touched.
    56	- This **refines ADR 0007 D5/D8**: it specifies *how* the consolidation writer dedups (embedding-cluster → exact/edge/entailment authority → merge/supersede), while leaving the per-turn recall tail exact-only.
    57	- **Disposition vs edge (no-drops, clean partition).** Every claim gets exactly one *disposition* — a `novel` or a `merge` — recording where its record lands. `supersede` is an *edge* layered on top: the superseding claim is disposed by its own novel/merge, and each superseded claim (plus its exact duplicates) is disposed by a `supersede`. The migration manifest proves this at the claim level: `accountReconciliation` fails the run (`complete: false`) if any eligible claim has zero dispositions (`unaccounted` — a silent drop) or more than one (`over_disposed` — an apply ambiguity). Quarantined claims carry no disposition.
    58	- Migration apply remains gated on Luke's full-ledger sign-off (P2 decision). No automated delete exists anywhere in the contract.
    59	
    60	## Amendment 1 (2026-06-23): decay-weight supersession + scope-gated render
    61	
    62	The original Decision 5 said a superseded record is "excluded from active recall (recall filters `status: active`)." Luke rejected the hard filter: *"how would recall know about other artifacts if they are not visible? this should rather be like temporal decay where it is weighted less if it's older / stale."* He approved three changes (verbatim sign-off, 2026-06-22):
    63	
    64	1. **Decay-weight, not hard-filter.** Extend the decay weight to factor `status` + `confidence`; superseded records stay reachable, ranked low. (See the revised Decision 5 score formula.)
    65	2. **Scope-gated render.** The `MEMORY.md` index is re-revised by dreaming, but **dormant projects are never re-revised** — gate the index/snapshot epoch bump on the per-scope consolidation watermark (token-waste avoidance).
    66	3. **ACL stays the only hard gate.** `sensitivity`/`visibility` are a security/privacy invariant and exclude before scoring; `status`/`confidence`/`age` only weight.
    67	4. **Deletion of superseded records is allowed via post-migration GC, not in the migration (added 2026-06-23).** Luke: *"I don't mind deleting superseded items."* Reconciled against point 1 by splitting the two axes — *staleness* (age) decay-weights and stays reachable; *supersession* (replacement) is deletable, because the superseding claim already carries the truth. The migration still **retains** superseded records (one-shot LLM judge is unproven there; retention = reversibility; the approved 0-dropped diff is unchanged). A later, explicitly human-triggered GC deletes records superseded beyond a grace window (`superseded_at` + N days). This refines the title's "supersede-not-delete" to: *reconcile never deletes; GC may, on a human's command, after the fact.* Implies an additive `superseded_at` timestamp on the supersede edge. (Deferred: GC policy + `superseded_at` field — later program phase.)
    68	
    69	### Why hard-filter is wrong, in one line
    70	
    71	A hard `status:active` filter and on-disk retention are contradictory: you pay to keep the record (audit, reversibility, "what did we believe before?") and then make it unreachable. Decay-weighting gets the only property the filter was protecting — *current truth ranks above stale* — without the unreachability.
    72	
    73	### External evidence (read-path comparison)
    74	
    75	- **mem0** — decay down-ranks, never deletes (recency ×1.5 / idle ×0.3, ~5× spread); decay layered on top of supersession. Matches the approved direction.

TARGET: Angle 1 — core qmd premise  
FLAW: No flaw in the premise. qmd’s CLI grammar allows only `lex`, `vec`, and `hyde` query lines, with collection as the only search scoping flag (`/Users/luke/.bun/install/global/node_modules/@tobilu/qmd/dist/cli/qmd.js:2980-3012`, `:3022-3040`). The HTTP `/query` endpoint accepts `searches`, `collections`, `limit`, `minScore`, `candidateLimit`, `intent`, and `rerank`, with no metadata/path/frontmatter predicate (`/Users/luke/.bun/install/global/node_modules/@tobilu/qmd/dist/mcp/server.js:532-558`). `searchMemoryHttp` likewise posts only `searches`, `collections`, `limit`, and `rerank` (`extensions/dream-memory/src/store.ts:1461-1469`).  
FIX/VERIFY: ADR 0010 should cite qmd CLI/API source or docs, not just `qmd query --help`.

2. SEVERITY: BLOCKER  
TARGET: ADR 0010 Decision 1 — harness visibility boundary  
FLAW: ADR 0010 makes `harness/<id>` provenance only, bundling all harness dirs into the same root collection (`docs/adr/0010-memory-scope-enforced-by-physical-partition.md:22-30`). That reverses ADR 0007’s explicit privacy boundary: visibility is not origin, new facts default origin-private, and ACLs stop “a Codex-captured client token surfacing as Pi or CC context” (`docs/adr/0007-unified-cross-harness-memory-store.md:38`).  
FIX/VERIFY: Either keep harness-private physical partitions, or explicitly amend ADR 0007 to accept cross-harness visibility as non-security-sensitive.

3. SEVERITY: CONCERN  
TARGET: Angle 2 — write-side correctness / misfiled notes  
FLAW: Dropping `scope` removes the independent backstop ADR 0007 intentionally kept: “scope frontmatter still records the distinction, so a misfiled note stays classifiable” (`docs/adr/0007-unified-cross-harness-memory-store.md:20`). `paths.ts` repeats the same invariant (`extensions/dream-memory/src/canonical/paths.ts:8-11`), while ADR 0010 explicitly says there will be “no independent intended-scope” left (`docs/adr/0010-memory-scope-enforced-by-physical-partition.md:77-80`).  
FIX/VERIFY: Keep an audit-only intended scope, or add writer-side path-vs-classification validation before removing `scope`.

4. SEVERITY: BLOCKER  
TARGET: Angle 3 — no-git-root sessions  
FLAW: ADR 0010 says project collection slug is `sanitize(gitRoot)` (`docs/adr/0010-memory-scope-enforced-by-physical-partition.md:22-26`, `:82`), but current code does not fail closed without git. `resolveProjectSlug` falls back to `normaliseSlug(basename(absCwd))` (`extensions/dream-memory/src/store.ts:1887-1902`) and anchors the slug map to `absCwd` when no git root exists (`extensions/dream-memory/src/store.ts:1907-1919`). A session in `~` or another non-repo dir can get an arbitrary project collection.  
FIX/VERIFY: Define and enforce no-git behavior: global-only unless `.dream-memory.yml` explicitly opts in, or require a real git root for `canonical-project-*`.

5. SEVERITY: SOUND  
TARGET: Angle 4 — mid-session registration vs span stability  
FLAW: No architectural flaw if ADR 0010 accepts the freshness delay. ADR 0010 resolves read-set once per session (`docs/adr/0010-memory-scope-enforced-by-physical-partition.md:46`) and auto-registers on first canonical write (`:48`); ADR 0008 says writes surface mid-session only via volatile recall and never mutate cached core (`docs/adr/0008-memory-cache-stability-contract.md:16-17`, `:26-28`). Same-session canonical recall delay is consistent with cache stability.  
FIX/VERIFY: Add a test that collection auto-registration does not mutate the current session read-set, and verify missing/unregistered collections degrade cleanly.

6. SEVERITY: UNVERIFIED ASSUMPTION  
TARGET: Angle 5 — secret separate-index feasibility  
FLAW: Named indexes are supported in qmd source: `--index <name>` exists (`/Users/luke/.bun/install/global/node_modules/@tobilu/qmd/dist/cli/qmd.js:3022-3024`), named indexes map to distinct SQLite files (`/Users/luke/.bun/install/global/node_modules/@tobilu/qmd/dist/store.js:418-435`), and daemon spawn propagates `--index` (`/Users/luke/.bun/install/global/node_modules/@tobilu/qmd/dist/cli/qmd.js:4023-4026`). But my-pi’s HTTP recall path has no index selector (`extensions/dream-memory/src/store.ts:1390-1414`), and ADR 0010 admits that plumbing does not exist (`docs/adr/0010-memory-scope-enforced-by-physical-partition.md:30`, `:80`). Concurrent default+secret daemon operation was not observed here.  
FIX/VERIFY: Prove two daemons/two ports/two indexes end to end before committing secrets to this design.

7. SEVERITY: CONCERN  
TARGET: Angle 6 — GC eventual reindex race  
FLAW: ADR 0010 allows physical delete before qmd prune and asks recall to skip missing docs (`docs/adr/0010-memory-scope-enforced-by-physical-partition.md:50`, `:75`, `:81`). That weakens ADR 0008’s tombstone-first rule: qmd must exclude tombstoned records before ranking (`docs/adr/0008-memory-cache-stability-contract.md:26-28`). It also leaves Tier 1 risk: ADR 0009 says `MEMORY.md` renders active records only and is scope-gated (`docs/adr/0009-memory-reconciliation-contract.md:27-30`, `:64-67`), so a physical-delete-before-rerender window can leave stale snapshot/core references.  
FIX/VERIFY: Tombstone first, qmd-filter before ranking, then physically prune only after qmd update plus scope snapshot/watermark rerender.

8. SEVERITY: BLOCKER  
TARGET: Angle 7 — migration/reconcile `.scope` contract  
FLAW: ADR 0010 says path will populate a sidecar `scope` column and consumers will stop reading the flag (`docs/adr/0010-memory-scope-enforced-by-physical-partition.md:36`). Current code is not there. `CanonicalFrontmatterSchema` requires `scope` (`extensions/dream-memory/src/canonical/frontmatter.ts:75-85`), serialization emits it (`extensions/dream-memory/src/canonical/serialize.ts:15-26`, `:57-66`), migration apply builds and parses it (`extensions/dream-memory/src/migration/apply/map-claim.ts:101-146`), and reconciliation treats `scope` as the blocking key (`extensions/dream-memory/src/reconcile/types.ts:14-22`, `extensions/dream-memory/src/reconcile/cluster.ts:5-13`, `extensions/dream-memory/src/reconcile/reconcile.ts:166-172`).  
FIX/VERIFY: Make sidecar/path-derived scope a real API first, migrate all consumers, then remove frontmatter `scope`.

9. SEVERITY: BLOCKER  
TARGET: Canonical collection naming / cutover drift  
FLAW: ADR 0010 chooses `canonical-global` and `canonical-project-<slug>` (`docs/adr/0010-memory-scope-enforced-by-physical-partition.md:22-25`), but current routing’s canonical shim uses `canonical-shared`, `canonical-harness-<id>`, and `canonical-episodic` (`extensions/dream-memory/src/active-memory/recall-routing.ts:41-60`) and is default-off dual-read (`extensions/dream-memory/src/active-memory/recall-routing.ts:63-76`). The qmd doc still says `pi-memory` is the active-memory default (`extensions/dream-memory/docs/qmd-collections.md:15-17`).  
FIX/VERIFY: Add an explicit migration table and update collection registration plus `recall-routing.ts` atomically.

10. SEVERITY: CONCERN  
TARGET: Angle 8 — federation cost  
FLAW: The stated `Promise.all(collections.flatMap(...))` fanout is not present in current `store.ts`; collections are sent as one array in one `/query` body (`extensions/dream-memory/src/store.ts:1437-1469`). The real latency multipliers are `extraQueries` fanout (`extensions/dream-memory/src/store.ts:1416-1423`, `:1544-1548`), hybrid lex+vector parallel search (`extensions/dream-memory/src/store.ts:1583-1596`), and route expansion into workspace/project-doc collections (`extensions/dream-memory/src/active-memory/recall-routing.ts:209-236`).  
FIX/VERIFY: Benchmark worst-case `resolveActiveRecallRoute + extraQueries + hybrid` before expanding read-sets beyond the two canonical collections.

11. SEVERITY: NIT  
TARGET: Adjacent status/recall doc drift  
FLAW: `frontmatter.ts` still says only `active` enters recall and superseded records are filtered (`extensions/dream-memory/src/canonical/frontmatter.ts:40-46`, `:93-96`), but ADR 0009 says superseded records stay reachable via per-turn recall and only ACL is a hard gate (`docs/adr/0009-memory-reconciliation-contract.md:27-30`, `:64-67`). This can mislead the ADR 0010 implementation work.  
FIX/VERIFY: Update the comments when ADR 0010 lands.

RECONSIDER
